title: sample-splitting-and-delimiter-coalescer-for-pin-stability
creator: Marco Diaz
description: Root-cause and mitigation work to prevent misaligned token boundaries and chat-template delimiter duplication that cause variability in token counts during model pinning and profile publish. This ticket implements a deterministic sample-splitting algorithm plus a delimiter coalescer that normalizes role/assistant/user markers during onboarding validation and pin rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarded model bundles no longer produce >1% variance in published per-request token counts across reproducible test corpus compared to baseline after pinning
Published performance profiles (latency/tokens/throughput) remain within 3% of synthetic benchmark once delimiter coalescer is enabled
Rollout includes a toggle to disable coalescer at runtime and automatically falls back to the previous tokenizer behavior without data-loss
Unit + integration tests covering edge cases: nested role markers, empty assistant messages, trailing/leading whitespace, subtoken splits near delimiter boundaries
Documented design and migration notes in Confluence and PR description, and an associated canary run executed against sandbox-dedicated pool
steps: Instrument failing onboarding messages and collect representative corpus from onboarding runs (see /dashboards/onboard-token-variance)
Design and implement 'sample-splitting' module that deterministically splits message streams into tokenization-safe chunks aligned to role delimiters
Implement 'delimiter coalescer' that merges adjacent/duplicate role markers (e.g., 'User:', ' user:' variations) into canonical markers prior to tokenization
Add a runtime flag `TOKEN_COALESCE=on|off` respected by onboarding validation and publish pipeline
Add telemetry to track pre/post token counts, token deltas per-message, and any fallback events
Create integration test harness that runs onboarding + profile publish in CI against a pinned model bundle to validate stability
Run controlled canary on sandbox-dedicated pool, analyze metrics, and perform rollback if token variance >1.5% or latency deviation >5%
decisions: Use deterministic greedy boundary heuristic for sample-splitting rather than attempting to replicate all model-specific tokenizer quirks — chosen to reduce complexity and improve predictability
Coalescer will operate on normalized Unicode and case-folded forms to catch common delimiter variants (e.g., 'Assistant:', 'assistant:')
Telemetry retention for these onboarding experiments set to 7 days in staging and 30 days in production for regression detection
Expose coalescer toggle at route-level in Console for enterprise customers to opt-out during initial rollouts
blocks: Waiting on kernel-level tokenizer shim from infra team (ENG-168999) for binary compatibility with quantized bundles
Need QA time to extend the onboarding harness — coordinate with Test Automation (assigned: Priya Rao)
test_plan: Unit tests for boundary heuristics (edge cases around punctuation and unicode),
CI integration test that runs publish pipeline against golden tokenization corpus,
A/B canary where 10% of onboarding traffic in sandbox uses coalescer and results compared
Manual exploratory QA on messages with deeply nested role blocks and multi-lingual markers
rollout_plan: Feature branch -> internal review -> CI passing -> canary on sandbox-dedicated pool for 72h
If canary metrics: token variance <1%, latency change <3% -> gradual ramp to 50% routes over 48h
Monitor console dashboards and abort/reroll to previous tag if any regression breach occurs
Enable route-level opt-out for first 2 weeks of rollout and collect customer feedback
notes: Observed failure pattern: small assistant messages with trailing markers caused tokenizer to emit an extra subtoken in 2 of 20 onboarding samples leading to profile delta
Related prior work: ENG-52199's template sanity checker reduced a class of template mismatches but didn't handle delimiter case coalescing
Trade-off: aggressive coalescing can mask upstream data-layer inconsistencies — we choose conservative rules to avoid changing user content semantics
